analysis.investment_thesis: Dhara Rail Pro fails the Magic Formula on both critical axes: earnings yield is a paltry ~3% (EBIT of INR 5 Cr against EV of ~INR 169 Cr), signaling a richly priced small-cap with no margin of safety. Worse, operating cash flow has been negative all three years, meaning reported earnings are not converting to real cash — the cardinal sin for a Magic Formula investor.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at ~27% CAGR (27→44 Cr), showing genuine demand for rail maintenance services.
Zero debt servicing cost (Finance Cost INR 0 Cr), keeping the income statement clean.
High promoter skin-in-the-game at 74.56%, aligning management incentives with the business.
key_risks: Earnings quality is hollow: Other Income (INR 4 Cr) nearly equals Operating Income (INR 5 Cr) — strip it and the core business barely earns anything.
OCF negative for 3 consecutive years (-2, -2, -5 Cr) — reported profits are not translating into cash; this destroys the Magic Formula premise.
Micro-cap at INR 148 Cr with extremely thin earnings base; any revenue miss or working-capital stretch could wipe out profitability entirely.
red_flags: Earnings Yield ≈ 3% (EBIT INR 5 Cr / EV ~INR 169 Cr) — far below the 12% Magic Formula minimum.
Free Cash Flow negative all three years; Net Profit of INR 7 Cr in 2025 vs OCF of -INR 5 Cr is a 12 Cr gap — classic earnings-quality red flag.
Other Income of INR 4 Cr in FY25 is 57% of net profit; core operating ROIC is well below the reported ROCE of 19%.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT is INR 5 Cr (operating income; I exclude Other Income of INR 4 Cr as non-recurring/non-operational). Enterprise Value = Market Cap INR 148 Cr + Debt INR 21 Cr ≈ INR 169 Cr. Earnings Yield = 5/169 = 3.0% — deeply below the 12% threshold where Greenblatt gets interested. Invested capital (Equity INR 20 Cr + Debt INR 21 Cr = INR 41 Cr) gives ROIC of roughly 12%, barely at the minimum floor. Both legs of the Magic Formula are weak-to-failing.

The cash flow picture makes it worse. A company reporting INR 7 Cr net profit while burning INR 5 Cr in operating cash flow — three years running — has a structural working-capital problem or is recognising revenue it hasn't collected. The INR +17 Cr investing inflow in FY25 looks like asset liquidation, not business compounding. The headline ROE of 50% is an artifact of the company's tiny prior equity base (INR 3 Cr in FY23), not evidence of durable capital efficiency. At a P/E of 36x on earnings that are largely non-operational and not cash-backed, there is no margin of safety here whatsoever.
